mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW 1 Series 135i engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW 1 Series 135i engine replacement typically costs £4,000-£8,500 for a reconditioned or rebuilt N55 or B58 unit supply-only. With supply and fit, expect £5,000-£10,000 depending on the specialist and location.

mainEntity.name: What engine is in the BMW 135i?

acceptedAnswer.text: The BMW 135i is powered by a 3.0-litre turbocharged straight-six petrol engine. Early E82/E88 models (2010-2012) use the N55B30A producing 306 hp and 400 Nm of torque. The F20/F21 M135i (2012-2015) uses the N55B30M0 producing 320 hp and 450 Nm of torque. Late F20 models (2015-2016) use the B58B30 producing 326 hp.

The N55 engine in the BMW 135i is generally regarded as reliable, though not as bulletproof as the naturally aspirated N52. Common issues include oil leaks (valve cover gasket, oil filter housing gasket), VANOS solenoid failure, and water pump failure. The B58 is more reliable but early production examples (2016-2018) can suffer from oil pump drive gear issues. Unlike the N20, the N55 does not have widespread timing chain issues.

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW 1 Series 135i engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW 1 Series 135i engine replacement typically takes 2-4 days for a specialist to complete, including removal of the old N55/B58 unit and fitting the replacement. The complexity of the six-cylinder turbo engine means labour time is higher than for four-cylinder models.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the BMW 135i and M135i?

acceptedAnswer.text: The BMW 135i and M135i are essentially the same car but with different naming conventions across generations. The E82/E88 135i (2010-2013) was never officially an M model, while the F20/F21 M135i (2012-2016) carried the M badge. Both use the N55 engine, but the M135i produces 320 hp compared to the E82's 306 hp.

mainEntity.name: Does a BMW 1 Series 135i rebuilt engine come with a warranty?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - every rebuilt BMW 1 Series 135i engine supplied through EnginesMarket comes with a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty. This covers the engine against manufacturing defects and component failure, giving you peace of mind when investing in a replacement N55 or B58 unit.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW 1 Series 135i - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW 135i was launched in 2008 as the performance flagship of the first-generation 1 Series range, powered by a 3.0-litre twin-turbo N54 engine. In 2010, the N54 was replaced by the N55 - BMW's first production engine to combine a single twin-scroll turbocharger with Valvetronic and direct injection. The 135i badge continued through the E82 coupe, E88 convertible and into the F20 hatchback as the M135i, before being replaced by the M140i with the B58 engine in 2016.

milestones.description: N54B30, 3.0L twin-turbo straight-six, 306 hp, launched in the E82 coupe and E88 convertible
N55B30A, 3.0L single twin-scroll turbo straight-six, 306 hp, replaces the N54 in the E82/E88 135i
N55B30A, 3.0L single turbo straight-six, 320 hp, launched in the F20 five-door and F21 three-door M135i
B58B30, 3.0L single twin-scroll turbo straight-six, 326 hp, introduced in later F20 M135i models
M135i renamed M140i with B58 engine; the 135i badge is retired in the UK

commonProblems.h2: BMW 1 Series 135i Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW 1 Series 135i is powered by 3.0-litre turbocharged straight-six engines across its production life. Early cars use the N55 (and earlier N54), which is generally reliable but has well-documented issues with oil leaks, VANOS solenoids, and the cooling system. Later B58-powered cars are more robust but have their own early-production concerns, particularly around the oil pump drive system. Replacement demand for the BMW 135i is typically lower than for four-cylinder BMWs, but when failures occur, the cost of repair can be significant. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Oil Leaks - Valve Cover, Oil Filter Housing and VANOS Solenoid Seals
problems.rootCause: The N55 engine uses gaskets and seals that can become brittle and leak over time. The valve cover gasket, oil filter housing gasket, and VANOS solenoid seals are the most common leak points. A leaking valve cover gasket can cause oil to drip onto the exhaust manifold, producing a burning smell and smoke. On the N54 and N55, multiple leak sources in close proximity can make it difficult to identify the primary source.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace valve cover gasket and PCV components

repairOptions.longevity: Address oil leaks before they cause further issues

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete rebuilt unit with new gaskets and seals

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2010-2015 BMW 1 Series 135i is currently valued at approximately £8,000-£18,000 depending on mileage, condition and body style (coupe and convertible models command a premium). This places the 135i firmly in the bracket where a rebuilt engine is a viable investment - replacement cost is typically small relative to vehicle value. For well-maintained, lower-mileage examples (especially M Sport or coupe models) worth £12,000+, a reconditioned or rebuilt engine with warranty is a sound investment.
problems.recommendation: The N55 is a reliable engine, and oil leaks are the most common issue. Address gasket leaks promptly - a £300-£600 specialist repair is far cheaper than dealing with the consequences of a major oil leak. If you notice white smoke or a burning smell, have the valve cover gasket inspected immediately. Unlike the N20, the N55 does not have widespread timing chain issues, making it a more dependable choice for long-term ownership.

problems.rootCause: The N55's VANOS system uses solenoids to control variable valve timing. These solenoids can become clogged or fail, leading to rough idling, reduced power and engine warning lights. Valvetronic eccentric shaft wear is another known issue - if the motor worm gear becomes damaged, the likelihood that the gears on the eccentric shaft are damaged increases. In severe cases, the eccentric shaft can wear into the cylinder head, requiring head replacement or a new engine.

problems.recommendation: VANOS and Valvetronic issues are usually repairable without engine replacement. A diagnostic scan will identify if fault codes are present. Cleaning or replacing the solenoids is a straightforward job for a specialist. If Valvetronic motor failure is detected, have the eccentric shaft inspected - catching wear early can prevent a much more expensive repair.

problems.group: Electric Water Pump & Cooling System Failure
problems.h4: Electric Water Pump & Cooling System Failure
problems.rootCause: The N55 uses an electric water pump that can fail without warning. Unlike belt-driven pumps, an electric pump failure may not be preceded by a visible leak. If the pump fails, the engine can overheat rapidly, potentially causing head gasket failure or worse.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace electric water pump and thermostat

repairOptions.longevity: If overheating has caused significant damage

problems.recommendation: Water pump and thermostat replacement is recommended as preventative maintenance around 80,000-100,000 miles. If your 135i has not had the water pump replaced, consider doing so proactively - it's significantly cheaper than dealing with an overheated engine.

problems.h4: B58 Oil Pump Drive Gear Failure (Early Production)
problems.rootCause: Early production B58 engines (2016-2018) have reported oil pump drive gear issues, particularly under high-stress driving. The oil pump chain guide used plastic components that can break under normal operating stress. A distinctive humming or whining noise from the engine, especially during cold starts, can indicate oil pump failure.

repairOptions.longevity: If oil pump failure has caused engine damage

problems.recommendation: If your B58-powered 135i produces a humming or whining noise from the engine on cold start, have the oil pump drive system inspected immediately. Early detection can prevent catastrophic engine failure. BMW has repaired this issue under warranty for many affected vehicles, but if your car is out of warranty, a specialist repair is significantly cheaper than a full engine replacement.

finalCta.h4: Don't Let Engine Failure Write Off Your BMW 1 Series 135i
finalCta.paragraph: The N55 engine in your BMW 135i is one of BMW's most celebrated turbocharged straight-sixes - a reliable, characterful engine that deserves proper maintenance. Oil leaks, VANOS issues and water pump failure are the most common problems, and all are repairable without replacing the entire engine in most cases. Later B58-powered cars are more robust but require vigilance for early oil pump issues.
